metaTitle: Best Portable Clothes Drying Racks in 2026
metaDescription: Five portable clothes drying racks compared on weight, folded size, stated load and garment capacity, so you can air dry laundry anywhere at home.
introParagraphs: A portable drying rack earns its place by moving easily from room to room, then disappearing into a closet. The five picks here span a wide range: the SpaceHidden folds to just 4 inches thick and is listed at 35 pounds, the Bobikuke weighs 4.7 pounds and folds to 3.5 inches thick, and the HOMIDEC offers 12 rods of 28 inches each for 22 to 32 garments.

The details separate them. The ZOES weighs about 5 pounds and stands 37.5 inches high, the LIENAHU is a tripod with 16 solid beech poles, and the SpaceHidden telescopes from 17.7 inches. Only the SpaceHidden states a clear load figure, which is worth noting for anyone drying towels or jeans.

We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback, weighing weight, folded size, stated load and drying capacity. The ranking favors racks that are light enough to carry with one hand, slim enough to hide, and clear enough about their limits that you know what they can safely carry.

products.name: SpaceHidden Foldable Clothes Drying Rack
products.description:
The SpaceHidden Foldable Clothes Drying Rack has a carbon steel frame with a rust resistant coating and ABS joints. It is listed to hold 35 pounds and folds flat to just 4 inches thick. The frame is telescopic, expanding from 17.7 inches.

It is described for compact laundry rooms, apartment balconies and humid bathrooms, and its stable X frame suits all three. The tradeoff is that 35 pounds is light for heavy towels and bedding, and the frame is less spread out than a rotating arm rack.

Because it folds to 4 inches, it hides behind a door or inside a closet. Carbon steel depends on its coating, so wipe it dry and check for chips. Compared with the Bobikuke, which weighs 4.7 pounds and states no load, the SpaceHidden gives a clearer load figure for less money.
pros: Folds flat to only 4 inches thick
Lowest cost pick in this guide
cons: 35 pounds is light for heavy towels
Coating chips can expose carbon steel

products.name: HOMIDEC 12 Rod Foldable Drying Rack
products.description:
The HOMIDEC Foldable Portable Laundry Drying Rack has 12 poles, each 28 inches long, with sock clips included. The listing says it holds 22 to 32 garments. It measures 30 by 29.1 by 37 inches and is made of steel with ABS accessories.

The accordion style design folds or sets up in one step. This is the highest capacity portable pick here, and the 28 inch rods give plenty of room. The tradeoff is a bigger footprint than the basic accordion racks and hinge points that can pinch fingers.

When folded it stores flat in a closet, though a 30 inch frame still needs a spot. Next to the SpaceHidden, it holds many more garments but does not state a pound rating, so spread the load and avoid heavy wet items on one end.
products.bestFor: Families who dry a full load at once
pros: 12 rods of 28 inches for 22 to 32 garments
cons: Larger footprint than basic accordion racks

products.name: Bobikuke Foldable Extendable Drying Rack
products.description:
The Bobikuke Foldable Clothes Drying Rack is a portable extendable rack in white. Its maximum unfolded size is 29.5 by 14.5 by 41.8 inches, and its minimum unfolded width is 17 inches. Folded, it measures 17 by 20.5 by 3.5 inches.

It is made of steel with ABS parts and weighs just 4.7 pounds, so it is easy to carry and fits in a car. This is the pick for road trips and for moving between rooms.

The extendable width lets you use a narrow rack for small loads and open it up when needed. Steel and ABS parts are described as withstanding sun exposure. Compared with the ZOES, it is a little lighter and extends, while the ZOES lists a single set size.
products.bestFor: Road trips and moving between rooms
pros: Fits in a car for travel
cons: No load rating in the listing

products.name: ZOES HOMEWARE Enhanced Clothes Drying Rack
products.description:
The ZOES HOMEWARE Enhanced Clothes Drying Rack measures 29 by 11.5 by 37.5 inches and weighs about 5 pounds. It is a collapsible rack aimed at apartments and small spaces. The listing says reinforced materials boost its load capacity by more than 100 percent compared with earlier versions.

The short 37.5 inch height makes it easy to reach, and the compact footprint saves space. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no published load rating and capacity is limited for big loads.

It collapses for storage and is easy to carry at about 5 pounds. The reinforced claim is relative, so treat the number cautiously until the listing states a pound figure. Against the SpaceHidden, it is similar in size but gives no pound rating, so the SpaceHidden is the safer buy if load matters.
pros: Short 37.5 inch height is easy to reach

products.name: LIENAHU Tripod Clothes Drying Rack
products.description:
The LIENAHU Clothes Drying Rack Tripod is a floor standing triangular rack with 16 poles made of solid beech. It collapses for storage and can sit in a corner, against a wall or at an angle. The listing says the beech poles resist aging and bending.

You can lay items flat for airflow or hang them, so it handles a range of fabrics. The tradeoff is that wooden poles need to be kept from sitting wet, and the listing gives no weight rating.

The tripod shape spreads items around the frame, which helps airflow. Wipe the poles dry after damp laundry so the wood stays in good shape. Next to the SpaceHidden, it trades a stated load rating and a 4 inch fold for a wooden look.
products.bestFor: Living rooms where a rack stays on display
pros: Fits corners, walls or angled spots
Lets you hang or lay items flat
cons: No weight rating in the listing

buyingCriteria.criterion: Stated load and what it assumes
buyingCriteria.explanation: Wet laundry is heavy, and one guide suggests planning for 10 to 15 pounds per load. The SpaceHidden states 35 pounds, while the ZOES, HOMIDEC, Bobikuke and LIENAHU give no pound figure. A rating of 30 pounds or more suits standard use and 50 pounds or more suits jeans, towels or bedding. Ratings assume even weight distribution, so spread heavy items and verify the figure on the manufacturer listing.

Capacity comes from how much rod you can use. The HOMIDEC has 12 rods of 28 inches, which is 28 feet in total and is listed for 22 to 32 garments. One guide says about 40 feet of rod handles roughly two loads, so a single HOMIDEC covers a bit over half of that. Add up rods before buying, and match the total to how much you wash at once.

A rack you cannot store ends up in the middle of the room. The SpaceHidden folds to 4 inches thick and the Bobikuke folds to 17 by 20.5 by 3.5 inches. Slim racks hide behind doors or in closets. Decide where the rack will live before you choose.

A portable rack must be easy to move with wet clothes on it, so carry weight matters. The Bobikuke weighs 4.7 pounds and the ZOES weighs about 5 pounds, which makes either easy to lift. A heavier frame is more stable but harder to carry. Choose a light rack if you move it often, especially if you have limited grip strength.

The frame shape decides how air moves around clothes. The SpaceHidden uses an X frame, the HOMIDEC has accordion rods and the LIENAHU is a tripod that can lay items flat. Indoor drying should finish within about a day and humidity should stay around 40 to 60 percent. Keep items spaced apart and place the rack near a window or fan.

The SpaceHidden is carbon steel with a rust resistant coating, the HOMIDEC and Bobikuke are steel with ABS parts, and the LIENAHU is solid beech. Coated steel is cheaper than stainless, but a chipped coating lets moisture reach the metal and rust. Wood needs to be wiped dry so it does not stay damp. Inspect the finish every few months and dry the rack after damp loads.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated load and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated loads, with the SpaceHidden's 35 pounds as the only clear figure. Racks that give no pound rating scored lower on confidence. Stable frames such as X frames and tripods scored higher for steadiness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at carry weight, from the Bobikuke's 4.7 pounds to the ZOES's 5 pounds. Lighter racks scored higher for moving between rooms. We also considered whether the rack stays steady once loaded.

howWeEvaluated.title: Folded size
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared folded thickness, including the SpaceHidden's 4 inches and the Bobikuke's 3.5 inches. Racks that hide easily scored higher. A rack that stays bulky when folded scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drying capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted rods and listed garment capacity, such as the HOMIDEC's 12 rods and 22 to 32 garments. More capacity means fewer loads in a day. We balanced capacity against footprint.

howWeEvaluated.title: Strongest versus most basic pick
howWeEvaluated.description: We set the HOMIDEC, with its 12 rods and one step fold, against the ZOES, the most basic and compact option. The SpaceHidden shows how a low cost rack can still state a clear load. Our analysis is based on product specs and buyer feedback, not hands on measurement.

howToChoose.subheading: For Travel and RV Use Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Choose a rack that is light and folds slim, since space in a car or RV is limited. Check the folded size and weight, and make sure it opens without tools. Capacity matters less than portability here.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Bobikuke weighs 4.7 pounds and folds to 3.5 inches thick, and its listing says it fits in a car. The SpaceHidden is the alternative when you want a stated 35 pound load.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You dry a full load often. The HOMIDEC's 12 rods and 22 to 32 garment capacity justify its upper range cost, and the LIENAHU suits a rack that stays on display.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your loads are small. The SpaceHidden is the lowest cost pick with a 35 pound rating, and the Bobikuke covers travel at low cost.

faq.q: How do I choose between a portable rack and a wall mounted one?
faq.a: Pick a portable rack if you want to move it to a window or fan, or if you rent. The SpaceHidden folds to 4 inches thick and the Bobikuke weighs just 4.7 pounds, so storage is easy. A wall rack needs drilling and stays in one place.

faq.q: Are portable drying racks worth the cost over a dryer?
faq.a: They are worth it for delicates and for saving energy, and the lowest cost option here is the SpaceHidden. The tradeoff is time, because indoor drying should finish within about a day. Many people use a rack for delicates and a dryer for towels.

faq.q: How much can a portable drying rack hold?
faq.a: The SpaceHidden states 35 pounds and the HOMIDEC lists 22 to 32 garments, while the other three give no stated load. Wet laundry is heavy, so plan for 10 to 15 pounds per load as a minimum. Ratings assume even weight distribution, so spread heavier items across the rods.

faq.q: How do I keep a metal rack from rusting?
faq.a: Wipe it dry after damp loads and check the coating for chips. The SpaceHidden is carbon steel with a rust resistant coating, and a chipped coating lets moisture reach the metal. Keep it out of standing water in a bathroom.

faq.q: Can I use a portable rack outdoors?
faq.a: The Bobikuke is described as withstanding sun exposure, and the SpaceHidden is described for balconies. Outdoor drying saves energy and gives clothes a fresh smell. Bring the rack inside when rain is likely.

faq.q: How long should laundry take to dry on a rack?
faq.a: Indoor drying should finish within about a day, or a mildew smell can start. Space items apart and place the rack near a window or fan. An extra spin cycle before hanging also cuts drying time, and thick towels and jeans set the real limit.
